facts.text: The README states that MuJoCo sends joint and sensor data over ROS topics and receives torque or position command data over ROS topics.

The documented publishers are /mujoco_ros_interface/joint_states (sensor_msgs/JointState), /mujoco_ros_interface/sensor_states (mujoco_ros_msgs/SensorState) and /mujoco_ros_interface/sim_time (std_msgs/Float32).
The documented subscribers are /mujoco_ros_interface/sim_command_con2sim (std_msgs/String) and /mujoco_ros_interface/joint_set (mujoco_ros_msgs/JointSet).
The README documents /mujoco_ros_interface/applied_ext_force (mujoco_ros_msgs/applyforce) with a link index, a force and a torque.
main subscribes the sim_command_con2sim String command topic and the applied_ext_force topic, and advertises sim_command_sim2con.
The node builds topic names from the /mujoco_ros_interface prefix, inserts a non-root node namespace, and appends /joint_set, /joint_states, /sim_time and /sensor_states.
joint_set is subscribed with queue size 1 and tcpNoDelay(true); joint_states, sim_time and sensor_states are advertised with queue size 1; pub_mode instead advertises SimStatus.

jointset_callback compares msg->time with mjData.time, accepts it only when it is not in the future and its age is at most 0.01 s, then copies msg->torque when MODE is 1 or msg->position when MODE is 0 into command[] for the loaded model's m->nu actuators.
jointset_callback sets cmd_rcv before its time checks; a command older than 0.01 s only logs an error, so cmd_rcv stays true and command[] keeps the previous values.
In both modes the size check compares joint_set_msg_.torque.size(), the node's own message buffer, with m->nu before copying m->nu entries of the received array.
state_publisher_init resizes joint_set_msg_.position and joint_set_msg_.torque to m->nu.
JointSet.msg declares Header header, float64 time, int32 MODE, float64[] position and float64[] torque, with MODE 0 documented as POSITION and MODE 1 as TORQUE.

state_publisher_init sizes the command arrays from m->nu and the JointState arrays from m->nu, m->njnt or the six virtual base entries, and creates an extra user-information sensor entry of two values.

state_publisher sets sim_time.data from mjData.time, publishes JointState position, velocity and effort from qpos, qvel and qacc, and publishes SensorState values from mjData.sensordata; the trailing user information entry holds dif_time and com_time.
The sim_command_callback handles RESET and INIT controller handshakes, toggles settings.run on 'pause', sets reset_request on 'mjreset', and publishes no acknowledgement on sim_command_sim2con.
rosPollEvents calls c_reset when reset_request is true.
c_reset calls mj_resetData, copies the selected keyframe time/qpos/qvel/act, and clears cmd_rcv.

c_reset calls mujoco_ros_connector_init, which publishes RESET and waits up to 1.0 s for the controller's RESET reply, then publishes INIT and waits up to 1.0 s for its reply before restoring the control callback.
mycontroller calls ros::spinOnce, publishes state only while settings.run, and copies the cached command into d->ctrl only when cmd_rcv is set.
The simulate thread steps physics only inside the settings.run branch and otherwise runs the paused branch.
mjData.time is the simulation time.
mjData stores qpos as position (nq values), qvel as velocity (nv values) and qacc as acceleration (nv values).
The README installation step clones the repository into a catkin workspace src directory and builds it with catkin_make.
mujoco_ros/package.xml declares catkin build and exec dependencies on roscpp, std_msgs and mujoco_ros_msgs.
The CMake project finds roscpp, std_msgs, mujoco_ros_msgs and eigen_conversions and includes the vendored mujoco210 headers.
The mujoco_ros package manifest declares its license as TODO.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned transport; no simulation step, pacing, trajectory or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free analytic contract transport: it answers the declared joint_states, sensor_states and sim_time subscriptions and records joint_set publications; it runs no MuJoCo, mj_step, controller, actuator, contact, sensor or ROS graph

joint names, positions, velocities, accelerations, sensor names and sensor data are fixed placeholders; the real arrays are sized by the loaded MJCF model (m->nu, m->njnt, m->nsensor and m->sensor_dim), and the fake returns smaller placeholder arrays
the fake does not advance mjData.time, integrate a command or echo a measured response; a joint_set publication is recorded but produces no motion
no wall-clock pacing; there is no reset, pause or snapshot/restore capability
the package deliberately leaves /mujoco_ros_interface/sim_command_con2sim, /mujoco_ros_interface/applied_ext_force and the shared-memory mode out of scope
a live run needs the operator's mujoco_ros node, loaded MJCF model and rosbridge; endpoint namespace, model dimensions, message sizes and the simulator build were not exercised

upstream defects at the pin: the joint_set size check reads the node's own buffer (always m->nu), so a shorter received array is read past its end, and a command older than 0.01 s leaves cmd_rcv set, so the previously accepted command keeps being applied; the fake models neither
the observation values carry no unit because the clone states none for the generalized coordinates and sensor data

safe_state.description: No acknowledged stop exists in the pinned clone: the only stop-like inputs are the unacknowledged 'pause' toggle and the 'mjreset' keyframe reset on /mujoco_ros_interface/sim_command_con2sim, so the MHS software latch cannot confirm that the simulator stopped. A zero JointSet publication is also only transmission.
